# NYCuriosity Data

> Charts behind NYCuriosity's posts plus civic tools: Council legislation trackers, community board leaders, and agency budgets, with member email alerts.

## NYC civic reference tools

- [How to Be an Effective NYC Community Board Member, NYCuriosity](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/cb_member_guide/): A presentation deck from NYCuriosity: how to be an effective member of your NYC community board. Structure, Robert's Rules, resolutions, the District Needs Statement, and the effectiveness playbook.
- [Obligations Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/legislation_implementation_tracker/): Every enacted NYC local law tells city agencies to do something. This tracker extracts each required action from the legislation text: the agency, the deliverable, and the deadline.
- [NYC Council Fiscal Impacts Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/nyc_council_fiscal_impacts_tracker/): Explore estimated fiscal impacts of NYC Council legislation: costs, revenues, and net fiscal impacts by agency and council member.
- [NYC Council Legislation Trackers](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/nyc_council_legislation_trackers/): Three trackers built from NYC Council legislation: what every law costs, requires of city agencies and allows them to do, with agency and council member profiles.
- [NYS Legislation Trackers](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/nys_legislation_trackers/): Every New York State bill since the 2009 legislative session, with sponsor, committee, status and chapter number for the laws that were signed.

## Community board tools

- [NYC Community Board Tools](https://data.nycuriosity.com/cb-tools/): Tools for New York City's 59 community boards: who serves on each board, how meetings should run, and four decades of searchable board resolutions.
- [Block Party: NYC Community Board Resolutions Dashboard](https://data.nycuriosity.com/cb-tools/block-party/): Resolutions from 26 Manhattan and Brooklyn community boards, searchable and downloadable on Block Party, plus the talks on how the archive was built.
- [From Public Records to Public Knowledge: Improving Access to Community Board Information — Block Party (NYC OMB Institute, July 2026)](https://data.nycuriosity.com/cb-tools/block_party_july2026/): Block Party's NYC OMB Institute talk on improving access to community board information, July 2026.
- [NYC Community Board Scorecard, All 59 Boards](https://data.nycuriosity.com/cb-tools/board-scorecard/): A prototype public dashboard for community board accountability across all 59 NYC boards: meeting lengths from 2,409 YouTube recordings, records coverage, and the 14 boards with no recordings at all.
- [AI Meeting Procedure Review: MCB3 June 2026](https://data.nycuriosity.com/cb-tools/meeting-review/): A working demo of AI meeting review: Claude analyzes the transcript of Manhattan CB3's June 2026 full board meeting against the City's parliamentary procedure guide, with coaching notes.
- [CB Member Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/cb-tools/member-tracker/): Who serves on all 59 NYC community boards: chairs, district managers, committees, rosters, and the term-limit clock behind upcoming openings.
- [Robert's Rules Helper for NYC Community Boards](https://data.nycuriosity.com/cb-tools/roberts-rules-helper/): A mid-meeting parliamentary procedure helper for NYC community boards: which motion you need, what to say, whether it needs a second, debate, or a vote — grounded in the City's official guide.
- [Building an AI-Powered Knowledge Base for NYC Community Boards — Block Party × NYCuriosity](https://data.nycuriosity.com/cb-tools/school-of-data-2026/): The School of Data 2026 talk on Block Party's community board resolutions database: what community boards are, why their resolutions matter, and how the searchable archive was built.

## Data behind NYCuriosity posts

- [COGE Report](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/coge_report/): Charts behind NYCuriosity's analysis of Mayor Mamdani's Commission on Government Efficiency: the five November ballot questions, and the procurement and technology reforms that did not make it onto the ballot.
- [Suggestions to Improve NYC Community Boards](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/community_board_suggestions/): Data behind NYCuriosity's community board reform article: all 59 board budgets, a decade of underfunding versus City Hall, and a 14-point reform table.
- [Council Obligations](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/council_obligations/): Charts from NYCuriosity's analysis of the administrative obligations NYC Council laws place on city agencies: 8,185 obligations extracted from 2,138 local laws enacted since 2014.
- [CSO Reports 2026](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/cso_reports_2026/): Data and charts from NYCuriosity's analysis of NYC Chief Savings Officer agency savings plans for FY2026 and FY2027.
- [G Train Weekend Shutdowns](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/g_train_weekend_shutdowns/): Data behind NYCuriosity's look at two years of G train weekend shutdowns: every closure weekend since 2023, who rides on Saturdays, CBTC timelines and costs, minutes lost.
- [Duties, Powers and Staffing: Legislation Trackers Update](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/legislation_trackers_update/): Four charts from the NYC Council Legislation Trackers: duties per power by agency, the types of powers, new duties against staffing, and powers by year.
- [Livable streets beyond Manhattan](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/livable_streets_cuf/): Traffic deaths by victim type, crashes in 55 districts, community board votes and Queens Boulevard injuries behind a livable streets forum recap.
- [Mamdani's First 100 Days](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/mamdani_100_days/): Data and charts from NYCuriosity's coverage of the April 7, 2026 Mamdani transition team panel: Rikers capacity, transit corridors, school funding, and DOT progress.
- [MCB3 History Analysis](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/mcb3_history_analysis/): Data and charts from NYCuriosity's analysis of MCB3 resolution history from 2002 to 2026 — topics, trends, and how the board's focus has shifted over time.
- [New York Needs to Grow](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/nyc_building_strategies/): Data and charts from NYCuriosity's look at NYC's new building era — transit expansion, construction costs, funding models, and the rezonings meant to tackle the affordability crisis.
- [NYC Labor Costs and the 2026 Bargaining Round](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/public_sector_unions_2026/): Six charts on what New York City spends on its workforce, what the budget reserves for new union contracts, and how unionized its public workers are.
- [QueensWay vs QueensLink](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/queensway_vs_queenslink/): Side-by-side comparison of the QueensLink rail reactivation proposal and the MTA's 2018 Rockaway Beach Branch sketch assessment. Ridership, costs, timeline, and methodology.
- [State Capacity Has a New Toolkit](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/state_capacity_ai/): Data and charts from NYCuriosity's look at how AI is reshaping state capacity: public service delivery, procurement, and federal regulation.
- [Local Law 195 Data](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/streets_plan_2026/): Fiscal impact, compliance tracking, and program breakdowns from NYC's 10-year streets plan under Local Law 195.
- [West 4th St Station Deep Dive](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/west_4th_st_station/): Data and charts from NYCuriosity's deep dive on West 4th Street–Washington Square: 94 years of history, ridership trends, hourly rhythms, and what subway construction cost then versus now.

## Optional

- [CB Alerts — CB Member Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/cb-tools/member-tracker/alerts/): Email alerts when an NYC community board you watch gets a new chair, district manager, committee chair, or roster change.
- [Board Profile — CB Member Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/cb-tools/member-tracker/board/): Leadership, committees, published roster, term clock, and recent decisions for an NYC community board.
- [Methodology & Coverage — CB Member Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/cb-tools/member-tracker/methodology/): Where the CB Member Tracker's data comes from, board by board: the CAU dataset, the Bronx BP roster, each board's own website, and what each source can and cannot say.
- [Upcoming Openings — CB Member Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/cb-tools/member-tracker/openings/): Term limits force the first citywide wave of NYC community board turnover on March 31, 2027. How the clock works and where seats are confirmed to expire.
- [Effective Community Board Member, One-Page Cheat Sheet, NYCuriosity](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/cb_member_guide/handout.html): A printable one-page cheat sheet on how to be an effective NYC community board member, from NYCuriosity.
- [Agency Workload — Obligations Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/legislation_implementation_tracker/agency-workload/): Which NYC agencies carry the most obligations from local laws enacted since 2014, ranked and broken down by deliverable type: rules, reports, programs, and outreach.
- [Member Tools — NYC Council Legislation Trackers](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/legislation_implementation_tracker/alerts/): Members get four tools built on the NYC Council Legislation Trackers: answers to questions from the tracker records, monthly email alerts, a brief for every council district, and a watchlist of changes.
- [Deadline Timeline — Obligations Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/legislation_implementation_tracker/deadline-timeline/): Statutory deadlines from NYC local laws in chronological order: what city agencies owe, when it is due, what is past due, and the recurring duties that never expire.
- [Law Explorer — Obligations Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/legislation_implementation_tracker/law/): Pick any NYC local law enacted since 2014 and see its full implementation checklist: every agency action it requires, with deadlines, statutory language, and Legistar links.
- [Methodology — Obligations Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/legislation_implementation_tracker/methodology/): How the Obligations Tracker works: where the law text comes from, what counts as an agency obligation, how quotes are verified, how deadlines are computed, and how agencies are identified and normalized.
- [Obligations Table — Obligations Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/legislation_implementation_tracker/obligations-table/): Every agency action required by NYC local laws enacted since 2014, in one filterable table: agency, deliverable, deadline, and the statutory language behind each obligation.
- [Powers Table — Powers Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/legislation_implementation_tracker/powers-table/): Every power New York City local laws enacted since 2014 grant to city agencies, from inspections to fees, listed apart from the duties agencies must deliver.
- [Powers Tracker — NYC Council Legislation Trackers](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/legislation_implementation_tracker/powers/): Every power New York City local laws enacted since 2014 grant to city agencies, by agency, type, and year, kept apart from the duties agencies owe.
- [Agency Powers — Powers Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/legislation_implementation_tracker/powers/agency-powers/): Which NYC agencies hold the most powers granted by local laws enacted since 2014, ranked and split by type: rulemaking, enforcement, designation, programs.
- [Fiscal Impact by Agency — NYC Council Fiscal Impacts Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/nyc_council_fiscal_impacts_tracker/agency-fiscal-impact/): Total fiscal impact of NYC Council legislation grouped by city agency, filterable by committee, sponsor, year, and expense type.
- [Costs vs. Revenue — NYC Council Fiscal Impacts Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/nyc_council_fiscal_impacts_tracker/cost-revenue-breakdown/): The NYC Council bills with the largest annual costs, next to the bills that raise revenue, from the Finance Division's fiscal impact statements.
- [Fiscal Impact by Year Legislated — NYC Council Fiscal Impacts Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/nyc_council_fiscal_impacts_tracker/intro-year-impact/): Total fiscal impact of NYC Council legislation grouped by the year each bill was introduced, filterable by agency, committee, and expense type.
- [Methodology — NYC Council Fiscal Impacts Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/nyc_council_fiscal_impacts_tracker/methodology/): How the NYC Council Fiscal Impacts Tracker works: data sources, scraping, extraction, filters, and calculations.
- [Fiscal Impacts Overview — NYC Council Fiscal Impacts Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/nyc_council_fiscal_impacts_tracker/overview/): What NYC Council legislation costs the city: annual fiscal impact estimates for Council bills since 2014, by agency, sponsor, year and cost versus revenue.
- [Fiscal Impact by Prime Sponsor — NYC Council Fiscal Impacts Tracker](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/nyc_council_fiscal_impacts_tracker/sponsor-fiscal-impact/): Total fiscal impact of NYC Council legislation grouped by prime sponsor, filterable by agency, committee, year, and expense type.
- [Agencies — NYC Council Legislation Trackers](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/nyc_council_legislation_trackers/agencies/): Every New York City agency the Council's laws touch: the duties and powers laws give it, fiscal estimates, and its budget, staff, payroll, and capital projects.
- [Council Members — NYC Council Legislation Trackers](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/nyc_council_legislation_trackers/council-members/): A legislation profile for every NYC Council member since 2014: sponsored bills, fiscal impacts, agency obligations created, searchable by name and filterable by session, party, borough, and district, with a district map view.
- [Bill Explorer — NYS Legislation Trackers](https://data.nycuriosity.com/civic_reference/nys_legislation_trackers/bills/): Search and filter every New York State bill and resolution since 2009 by chamber, stage, committee and sponsor, with chapter numbers for signed laws.
- [How COGE's Twelve Study Areas Became Five Ballot Questions](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/coge_report/ballot-disposition/): COGE's preliminary report studied twelve areas of the City Charter. Seven reached the November ballot, three went to a future commission, franchises and concessions went back to FCRC rulemaking, and technology went to an appendix.
- [A NYC Alteration Permit Takes 15 Days. A New Building Takes 166.](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/coge_report/building-permits/): Median days from filing to first permit in DOB NOW: 15 days for a routine alteration, 166 days for a new building. The permits that produce housing wait the longest.
- [Only 39% of NYC Contracts Were Registered On Time](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/coge_report/contract-timeliness/): New York City registered just 39% of its contracts before their start date in FY2025, the best rate in five years. Nearly one in five landed more than 90 days late.
- [The Agency That Runs NYC Technology Takes 1,372 Days to Run an RFP](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/coge_report/cycle-time-by-agency/): Median RFP cycle times by New York City agency, FY2025. The Office of Technology and Innovation took 1,372 days, more than three times the citywide median of 387.
- [Whether a NYC Nonprofit Gets Paid On Time Depends on Which Agency Hired It](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/coge_report/nonprofit-payment/): On-time submission of human services contracts ranged from 8% at Small Business Services to 93% at the Administration for Children's Services in FY2025.
- [What a 12% Reserves Target Means: $9.8 Billion](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/coge_report/rainy-day-fund/): Ballot Question 5 sets a reserves target of 12% of City tax revenue. Against FY2026's $81.3 billion tax base that is $9.8 billion, roughly twice the revenue drop the City absorbed in FY2021.
- [A New York City RFP Takes a Median of 387 Days](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/coge_report/rfp-cycle-time/): The median competitive sealed proposal in New York City took 387 days end to end in FY2025. Evaluation and post-award review account for 234 of those days.
- [Ballot Question 3 Reaches 4,103 Vacant City Lots, and 5% of the Vacant Land](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/coge_report/street-safety-and-land/): Three quarters of New York City's 5,442 vacant lots are small enough for the expedited review Ballot Question 3 creates, but they hold only 262 of 4,908 vacant acres.
- [All 59 Community Board Budgets, FY2027](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/community_board_suggestions/board-budgets/): Every NYC community board's FY2027 adopted budget, ranked: a $234,000 spread between the best and worst funded boards, and a median of $383,130 to represent up to 200,000 people.
- [Community Board Budget Growth vs. City Hall, FY2017–FY2027](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/community_board_suggestions/budget-growth/): Over the decade to FY2027, the Mayor's Office budget grew 61% and the citywide budget 47%. Community board budgets grew 30%, roughly even with inflation.
- [14 Recommendations to Improve Community Boards](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/community_board_suggestions/recommendations-table/): The full reform table from NYCuriosity's community boards article: 14 recommendations across members, meetings, and structure, with who acts and what each one takes.
- [New Standing Obligations Per Year, 2014–2025](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/council_obligations/added-per-year/): The NYC Council adds hundreds of standing obligations to agency dockets every year: at least 250 in every year since 2015, and 509 in 2025, the most since 2019.
- [Obligations by Agency](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/council_obligations/agency-concentration/): Ten agencies carry 57% of the 6,589 obligations NYC local laws since 2014 assign to a specific agency; the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene leads with 581.
- [The Standing-Obligation Stack, 2014–2026](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/council_obligations/recurring-stack/): Recurring obligations from NYC Council laws never retire, so they stack: agencies carried 75 standing obligations from post-2014 laws at the end of 2014 and carry 4,972 today.
- [Report Filing Status by Agency](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/council_obligations/report-filing-status/): Of the 728 reports required by NYC local laws since 2014 that can be checked against the DORIS register, 214 have never been filed and 143 more are overdue.
- [Reports Due Every Year, 2014–2026](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/council_obligations/reports-every-year/): NYC agencies now owe 850 reports on at least an annual cadence under Council laws enacted since 2014, up from 17 at the end of 2014, 69 new recurring reports a year on average.
- [Agency Savings Breakdown — CSO Reports 2026](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/cso_reports_2026/agency-breakdown/): Sortable, searchable table of all 16 NYC agency Chief Savings Officer savings plans for FY26 and FY27, with FY25 budget context.
- [CSO Savings vs. IBO Budget Options](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/cso_reports_2026/ibo-comparison/): How NYC's Chief Savings Officer agency savings for FY26 and FY27 compare to IBO-identified budget options.
- [NYC Tax Rates — CSO Reports 2026](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/cso_reports_2026/nyc-tax-rates/): A breakdown of every major tax NYC imposes on residents and businesses — income, property, business, and more.
- [Savings by Category — CSO Reports 2026](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/cso_reports_2026/savings-by-category/): How NYC's $246M in CSO savings break down by type: eligibility audits, contract termination, renegotiation, revenue, and in-housing.
- [Weekend Bus Speeds on the G Corridor, 2023–2026](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/g_train_weekend_shutdowns/bus-speeds/): Monthly weekend average speeds for the B62, B43, B48 and B32, the bus routes that parallel the G train, January 2023 to June 2026: 7 to 8 mph, unchanged.
- [NYC Subway CBTC Signal Project Timelines, 2003–2029](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/g_train_weekend_shutdowns/cbtc-timelines/): Contract award, promised completion and delivered or projected date for seven NYC subway CBTC signal projects, Canarsie to Crosstown: every one late.
- [G Train Trips by Mode on a Shutdown Weekend](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/g_train_weekend_shutdowns/minutes-by-mode/): Scheduled G travel times for four station pairs against a shuttle bus at measured weekend speed, a Citi Bike and walking: Court Sq to Bedford-Nostrand is 16 minutes by train, 40 by bus.
- [Subway On-Time Performance Before and After CBTC](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/g_train_weekend_shutdowns/on-time-performance/): Monthly weekday on-time performance for the 7, L and G since 2015: the 7 jumped from 68% to 91% after CBTC signals activated in November 2018. The G runs at 80% today.
- [G Train Weekend Closures, 2023–2026](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/g_train_weekend_shutdowns/weekend-closures/): Every weekend the G train was shut on part of the Crosstown line since 2023, detected from station-level ridership: 15 of the first 34 weekends of 2026.
- [G Train Weekend Ridership by Station, 2025](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/g_train_weekend_shutdowns/weekend-ridership/): Median Saturday, Sunday and weekday entries in 2025 at the ten stations only the G serves, and what those stations record on shutdown Saturdays.
- [Duties per Power by Agency](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/legislation_trackers_update/duties-per-power/): DOB, DCWP and HPD receive one power for every two duties the NYC Council assigns them; DOT and DOHMH receive one for every 4.6. Ten agencies, 2014–2026.
- [New Duties vs. Planned Headcount](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/legislation_trackers_update/duties-vs-headcount/): DOB took on 193 new duties from NYC local laws since FY2022 while its planned headcount fell 7.6%. Twelve agencies compared, FY2022 to FY2027.
- [Powers by Type](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/legislation_trackers_update/powers-by-type/): Rulemaking accounts for 564 of the 1,706 powers NYC local laws have granted agencies since 2014; enforcement and inspection for 360.
- [Duties and Powers by Year Enacted](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/legislation_trackers_update/powers-per-year/): NYC local laws granted 152 new agency powers a year from 2014 to 2021 and 90 a year from 2022 to 2025, while new duties held near 630 a year.
- [Community board votes on street-safety items](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/livable_streets_cuf/cb-votes/): How Manhattan and Brooklyn community boards voted on 580 street-safety resolutions: Brooklyn boards opposed 14.1% of items, Manhattan boards 2.6%.
- [Traffic deaths by victim type](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/livable_streets_cuf/deaths-by-mode/): Annual NYC traffic deaths 2013 to 2025 split by pedestrians, cyclists and motorists, from NYPD crash data: 229 deaths in 2025, down from 297 in 2013.
- [Injury crashes by community district](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/livable_streets_cuf/district-crashes/): Change from 2021 to 2025 in crashes with an injury or death across NYC's 55 PUMA districts: 32 rose, including 14 of the 17 in Queens and Staten Island.
- [Queens Boulevard injuries, 2013 to 2025](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/livable_streets_cuf/queens-blvd/): Annual injuries on Queens Boulevard 2013 to 2025 and their share of all NYC traffic injuries: 507 injuries (0.92%) in 2013, 293 (0.59%) in 2025.
- [A Better Billion — All 12 Proposed Projects — Mamdani's First 100 Days](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/mamdani_100_days/better-billion-corridors/): All 12 subway expansion projects in the NYU Marron Institute's A Better Billion plan: 41 new miles, 64 new stations, 167,064 housing units over 40 years.
- [How NYC Uses Its Curb Space — Mamdani's First 100 Days](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/mamdani_100_days/dot-lane-progress/): About 62% of NYC's 12,000 linear curb miles are dedicated to car storage. Only 5% supports protected bike or bus lanes.
- [Rikers Population vs. Capacity — Mamdani's First 100 Days](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/mamdani_100_days/rikers-population/): Rikers Island average daily population vs. planned borough jail capacity, 2019–2025.
- [NYC School Funding by Source — Mamdani's First 100 Days](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/mamdani_100_days/school-funding/): How NYC's $38B DOE operating budget splits between city, state, and federal dollars — and which schools are most exposed to federal cuts.
- [311 Noise Spikes vs. MCB3 Resolutions](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/mcb3_history_analysis/311-vs-resolutions/): Did MCB3 resolutions lead or lag the 311 noise complaint explosion of 2020? A month-by-month look at the pandemic noise surge and the board's formal response.
- [MCB3 Resolutions vs. 311 Complaints by Agency](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/mcb3_history_analysis/agencies-comparison/): Which city agencies does MCB3 formally address vs. which agencies residents actually complain to? A side-by-side percentage comparison revealing where board attention and resident grievances diverge.
- [MCB3 Resolution Topics vs. 311 Complaints](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/mcb3_history_analysis/topics-comparison/): Side-by-side comparison of MCB3 resolution topics and CB3 311 complaint categories, revealing where board attention aligns with — and diverges from — resident concerns.
- [MCB3 Resolution Topics Over Time](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/mcb3_history_analysis/topics-over-time/): How the focus of MCB3 resolutions has shifted across topic categories from 2004 to 2025 — from SLA-dominant to a more diverse agenda.
- [City of Yes vs. Two Decades of Rezonings](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/nyc_building_strategies/city-of-yes-rezonings/): Projected housing units from City of Yes compared with each major NYC neighborhood rezoning since 2004.
- [The Most Expensive Track on Earth](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/nyc_building_strategies/construction-costs/): Subway construction cost per mile: New York's East Side Access and Second Avenue Subway vs. peer projects in London, Paris, Tokyo, Copenhagen, Milan, Seoul, and Madrid. PPP-adjusted 2023 dollars from the Transit Costs Project.
- [Ranking the MTA's Expansion Wishlist](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/nyc_building_strategies/expansion-rankings/): Every candidate expansion project in the MTA's 2023 20-Year Needs Assessment Comparative Evaluation, ranked by cost per minute of door-to-door travel time saved over 30 years.
- [How Transit Agencies Pay the Bills](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/nyc_building_strategies/funding-mix/): Operating revenue mix — fares vs. government subsidy vs. other income — for the MTA, Transport for London, and Hong Kong's MTR.
- [Projected Growth by NYC Spending Line, FY2026 to FY2030](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/public_sector_unions_2026/growth-by-line/): Health insurance and wages are set to grow faster than New York City's city-funded spending through fiscal 2030, while pension contributions fall 19%.
- [Personnel Costs as a Share of NYC's Adopted Budget](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/public_sector_unions_2026/labor-share/): Personal services fell from 54.1% of New York City's adopted expense budget in fiscal 2017 to 50.9% in fiscal 2027, per the City's Expense Budget data.
- [NYC Overtime: Record Spending and Budget Overruns](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/public_sector_unions_2026/overtime/): New York City overtime reached a record $2.85 billion in fiscal 2026, $299 million over budget, and overtime paid has nearly doubled since fiscal 2014.
- [NYC Pension Contributions After the 2026 Restructuring](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/public_sector_unions_2026/pension-contributions/): New York City's planned pension contributions fall from $9.6 billion in fiscal 2026 to $7.7 billion in 2030 after the State let it stretch out payments.
- [What NYC's Next Union Raises Cost Against the Labor Reserve](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/public_sector_unions_2026/raise-cost/): New York City's financial plan reserves 1.25% annual raises. Matching the last round's 3% would cost about $1 billion more with each contract year.
- [Public and Private Union Density in NYC, New York State and the US](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/public_sector_unions_2026/union-density/): In 2025-26, 65.1% of public sector workers in New York City were union members against 14.3% of private sector workers, per CUNY's State of the Unions.
- [QueensLink vs MTA 2018 Study — Comparison Table · NYCuriosity](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/queensway_vs_queenslink/comparison-table/): Side-by-side comparison of QueensLink proposal metrics vs. MTA's 2018 Rockaway Beach Branch sketch assessment. Capital cost, ridership, service design, and infrastructure.
- [Further QueensLink Facts & Figures · NYCuriosity](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/queensway_vs_queenslink/further-facts/): QueensLink's environmental, economic, and timeline projections for the Rockaway Beach Branch M-train extension: CO₂ reduction, car trips removed, economic output, job creation, and delivery schedule.
- [74 Years of Red Tape](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/state_capacity_ai/cutting-red-tape/): The Code of Federal Regulations grew from 9,745 pages in 1950 to 194,395 in 2024. The accumulation AI can finally help map and prune.
- [NYC's Contracts Arrive Late, and Later Every Year](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/state_capacity_ai/procurement-contracting/): By value, most NYC contracts are now registered after their start date, and the share keeps rising, hitting 85% for nonprofits in FY2024. The procurement chokepoint AI could help unblock.
- [The Same Benefit, Delivered Unequally](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/state_capacity_ai/public-service-delivery/): SNAP take-up ranges from 55% to 100% across states for the exact same federal benefit. Delivery is a capacity choice, and where AI service tools fit.
- [Plan 1 Compliance Tracker — Streets Plan 2026](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/streets_plan_2026/compliance/): How NYC DOT's actual annual delivery compared to the minimum benchmarks required by Local Law 195's first five-year plan.
- [10-Year Fiscal Impact — Streets Plan 2026](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/streets_plan_2026/fiscal-impact/): 10-year fiscal impact of Local Law 195 by plan period, broken down by expense, capital, and net costs above the existing DOT baseline.
- [LL195 Legislative Mandates — Streets Plan 2026](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/streets_plan_2026/ll195-mandates/): Minimum benchmarks set by Local Law 195 for each five-year plan period. Plan 1 was due December 2021; Plan 2 is due December 2026.
- [Program Cost Breakdown — Streets Plan 2026](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/streets_plan_2026/program-breakdown/): Program-by-program 10-year cost breakdown for Local Law 195, showing the additional cost above DOT's existing baseline for each mandate.
- [West 4th Street Annual Ridership, 2017–2025](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/west_4th_st_station/annual-ridership/): Annual ridership at West 4th Street–Washington Square: entries and estimated arrivals, from the 14M pre-pandemic peak through the COVID collapse to the 2025 recovery.
- [Subway Construction Costs, Then vs. Now](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/west_4th_st_station/cost-comparison/): What West 4th Street's construction era cost against the modern record: the 1932 IND and 1961 express tracks versus the 7 extension, Second Avenue Subway, East Side Access, and the IBX, in 2025 dollars.
- [West 4th Street Hourly Ridership Rhythms](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/west_4th_st_station/hourly-profile/): Hour-by-hour ridership at West 4th Street–Washington Square in 2025: arrivals versus departures, and how the station's late-night profile compares to Wall St, Grand Central, and Bedford Av.
- [West 4th Street Station Timeline, 1932–2026](https://data.nycuriosity.com/nycuriosity_substack_posts/west_4th_st_station/station-timeline/): Ninety-four years of West 4th Street–Washington Square: built in 1932 with a lower level for a line that didn't exist yet, completed in 1967, renewed in 2026.
